messages.author: c8be870b4307e743
messages.subject: multipleGroup and Missing Data
parts:
Hi Phil. I love your package and am using it for my dissertation. I asked a question on Github but then found this forum and thought it would be more appropriate. I know several past threads have asked about multiple groups and missing data, but didn't seem to provide an answer to my question.

I am wondering how multipleGroup handles missing data? Specifically, if some groups are not administered an item, I would assume multipleGroup drops those items from the group-level analysis. However, in running the code below, that group (D) has item parameters for items that were all NAs (items 5, 10, 15, and 20).

For context, I am re-estimating PISA data and for some countries, some items were not included. Additionally, I am doing this across cycles (I have cycle-by-country groups). Many items were not asked across cycles, meaning there will be many columns with complete NAs for certain cycle-by-country groups (e.g. 2006-USA, 2009-USA would have different complete columns).


```

library(mirt)

library(tidyverse) # simulate data ---- set.seed(1234) N <- 1000 # create covariates ---- X1 <- rnorm(N); X2 <- rnorm(N) Theta <- matrix(0.5 * X1 + -1 * X2 + rnorm(N, sd = 0.5)) # create items and response data ---- a <- matrix(1, 20); d <- matrix(rnorm(20)) dat <- simdata(a, d, 1000, itemtype = '2PL', Theta=Theta) # create groups ---- groups <- c(rep("A", 250),rep("B", 250),rep("C", 250),rep("D", 250)) # generate missing values in item data ---- # group A - 50 missing values dat_a <- dat %>% as.data.frame() %>% slice(1:250) for (i in 1:50) { dat_a[sample(nrow(dat_a),1),sample(ncol(dat_a),1)] <- NA } # group B - complete cases dat_b <- dat %>% as.data.frame() %>% slice(251:500) #group C - 100 missing values dat_c <- dat %>% as.data.frame() %>% slice(501:750) for (i in 1:100) { dat_c[sample(nrow(dat_c),1),sample(ncol(dat_c),1)] <- NA } # group d - 5 missing columns dat_d<- dat %>% as.data.frame() %>% slice(751:1000) %>% mutate_at(vars(5,10,15,20), ~NA) # combine data dat2 <- rbind(dat_a, dat_b, dat_c, dat_d) # model with missing item data mod0 <- multipleGroup(dat2, 1, group=groups,'2PL', invariance = c("slopes", "intercepts", "free_mean", "free_var")) summary(mod0)
```

Thank you!

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: multipleGroup and Missing Data
parts:
In isolation group D's parameters are not estimable, and the responses contribute no information about the parameters anyway. So, you may as well set them either a) as fixed at some arbitrary values and ignore them in the output (I'm less fond of that as it can be confusing, but certainly viable), or b) set them equal to some other parameters that are estimable to completely 'borrow strength' from other parameters that do have valid observations (which is what your code does via the invariance input). Make sense?

Phil

messages.subject: Re: multipleGroup and Missing Data
parts:
Thanks for your explanation. The `multipleGroup` function will not run with missing data unless invariance parameters are set. Is there any way to allow items with some missing data to borrow from other valid observations while ignoring items that are completely missing data?  My next step after item parameter estimation is to then use `fscores` to draw plausible values. I'm not sure if it is valid to have items with completely missing values contribute to plausible values. Though, I may not completely understand how the values are being drawn. 

Ultimately, I am running multi group on cycle-by country (e.g. 2006-USA, 2006-AUS, 2009-USA. 2009-AUS, etc) for 5 cycles and want to make sure my approach is correct. I can get around this by just estimating trend items, but I lose a lot of countries and information in the process. 

Thanks for your help!!

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: multipleGroup and Missing Data
parts:
The approach used by 'plausible' is to randomly draw a value from the approximated posterior distribution for each response vector implied by the model. The 'approximate' part is that the posterior is estimated with a Gaussian shape by default, and so a value is sampled according to the EAP and SD(EAP) information given fixed item parameters (more variable plausible scores could be obtained using MCMC to either estimate the individual posteriors more accurately in situations where Guassian approximations are unreasonable, or when you want to include the sampling uncertainty of the item parameter estimates in these plausible values as well). I haven't added full-blown MCMC support to the package yet, but perhaps will sometime in the future.

Phil
